### Also covered by

Riehl, *Category Theory in Context*, 2nd ed., Epilogue §E.1 ("Theorems in
context"), the restatement of the Yoneda lemma, printed p. 251 (PDF p. 271) —
item `riehl:E.1:thm-yoneda`.

Riehl states the bijection `Nat(C(-,c), F) ≅ F c` as *natural in both `c` and
`F`*, which is exactly this issue's obligation; everything else in her
restatement (evaluation at the identity, in both variances, plus the
represented-to-represented consequence that every transformation
`C(-,c) ⇒ C(-,c')` is postcomposition with a unique morphism) is already in
force in-tree via `Functor/Hom/Yoneda.v:133`/`:182`/`:231` and
`Functor/Hom.v:85`/`:96`/`:109`.

Phase-D sharpening worth carrying into the implementation: the verifier's blind
pass independently confirmed that **no** naturality square for the Yoneda
bijection exists anywhere, and eliminated the two plausible false positives —
`Theory/Coend/Yoneda.v` supplies only the apex-level ninja/co-Yoneda
isomorphisms, and `Structure/UniversalProperty.v:54` `preyoneda` is the
pointwise computation `τ_d f = P f (τ_c id)`, not a naturality statement. It
also checked the notation: `Instance/Sets.v:205` defines `x ≊ y` as
`{|carrier := x|} ~= [Sets] {|carrier := y|}`, so `Yoneda_Embedding` really is
the hom-setoid bijection and the represented-to-represented clause is genuinely
present.

- [ ] (from Riehl §E.1) LIBRARY-DEFECT: `Functor/Hom/Yoneda.v:18-22` presents
      the formalized result as "`Nat([Hom ─,A], F) ≅ F A`, natural in both `A`
      and `F`" and maps that display directly onto the in-tree encoding, but
      what is proved is a per-object family of setoid isomorphisms with no
      naturality in either variable. Either repoint the header at the natural
      isomorphism this issue builds, or state there explicitly that naturality
      is not formalized.

### Also covered by

Riehl, Epilogue §E.1, the restatement that representations are initial
(resp. terminal) objects of the category of elements, printed p. 252
(PDF p. 272) — item `riehl:E.1:thm-representation-initial`.

The Epilogue states exactly this issue's biconditional in both variances, so it
adds no new obligation. Phase-D sharpening for the implementer: the verifier
independently confirmed that "category of elements" occurs at exactly one place
in the whole tree — `Construction/Grothendieck.v:108`, a comment — that no file
matches `*element*`, and that the in-tree Grothendieck construction is indexed
by an `IndexedCat` (Cat-valued), never by a `Sets`-valued functor. It also
closed off the tempting shortcut: the comma `=(1) ↓ F` at the singleton setoid
*would* be the category of elements up to the global-elements isomorphism
`(1 ~> X) ≅ X` in `Sets`, but that isomorphism is also not in-tree, so even the
specialization route is unavailable until this issue's step 5 supplies it.

### Also covered by

Riehl, Epilogue §E.1, the restatement that a category with coproducts and
coequalizers has all colimits (and dually), printed p. 252 (PDF p. 272) —
item `riehl:E.1:thm-colimit-construction`.

Riehl states the colimit direction first and the limit direction as its dual;
this issue's Work item 2 already scopes both ("dually, coequalizers plus small
coproducts give `Cocomplete`"), so no additional obligation is created.

Phase-D sharpening the implementer should have: the verifier established a
stronger negative than the coverage record did — there is **no inhabitant of
`Complete` or `Cocomplete` over any concrete category anywhere in the tree**
(the sole consumer, `Theory/Adamek/Corollaries.v:61`, takes `Cocomplete` as a
hypothesis). So nothing in the library forces this construction to exist even
implicitly, and this issue would produce the first witnesses.

- [ ] (from Riehl §E.1) LIBRARY-DEFECT: `Structure/Limit.v:69-72` claims that
      "uniqueness up to unique isomorphism, preservation, construction from
      products and equalizers" are all things "proved once about `[Limit]`".
      Only preservation exists (`Structure/Limit/Preservation.v`): there is no
      limit-uniqueness-up-to-unique-isomorphism result (`limit_med_unique` /
      `limit_med_eq` at `Preservation.v:82`/`:93` are about the *mediator*, not
      about two limit apices), and the products-and-equalizers construction is

      is a separate claim from the `:94-103` prose already listed above.

### Also covered by

Riehl, Epilogue §E.1, the restatement of Freyd's size argument — a category
admitting products indexed by a collection larger than its own collection of
morphisms is a poset — printed p. 252 (PDF p. 272), item
`riehl:E.1:thm-large-products-poset`.

Riehl's phrasing is the "products larger than the cardinality of the morphism
collection" form rather than the "small and complete" form; it is the same
theorem and the same argument, and this issue's Work already states the
diagonalisation step in exactly that shape.

Phase-D sharpening the implementer must not lose: the verifier explicitly
weighed and **rejected** OUT-OF-SCOPE, on the ground that the statement is
expressible here — universe polymorphism already lets one quantify a product
over a hom-indexed family, as `Adjunction/SAFT.v:175-192` does with
`cogen_power_index`. That is the concrete in-tree precedent for the indexing
this issue needs. The verifier also flagged the constructivity caveat that
`Structure/Complete.v:104-106` records: Hyland's effective-topos counterexample
means the thinness theorem is **not** constructively provable, so the in-tree
statement must be scoped classically or restated (e.g. as a `P(Mor) → Hom`
injection contradiction under explicitly classical hypotheses). This issue's
Verification section already asks that any use of classical reasoning be
disclosed; that caveat is the reason.

### Also covered by

Riehl, Epilogue §E.1, the restatement of the adjoint functor theorems in three
clauses, printed p. 252 (PDF p. 272) — item `riehl:E.1:thm-gaft`.

Clauses (i) and (ii) of Riehl's statement are already fully in force in-tree,
and in a slightly stronger form than the book: `Adjunction/GAFT.v:180`
`GAFT_from_initials` needs neither completeness nor continuity, and
`Adjunction/GAFT.v:241` `GAFT`'s continuity hypothesis is the cone-level
`PreservesImageLimit`, which `Construction/Comma/Limit.v:264` shows every right
adjoint satisfies. The only gap is clause (iii) — the coseparating-set form —
which is this issue's subject.

Phase-D sharpening: the verifier re-derived the clause-(iii) gap independently
by reading `Adjunction/SAFT.v:240-250`. `SubobjectCover` is a **hypothesis**
asserting, for every `h : d ~> U c`, an index `i`, a map `s : d ~> U (sub_dom i)`
and a `t` with `fmap[U] t ∘ s ≈ h` — i.e. precisely the
image-factorization-through-a-subobject step that Riehl's "every collection of
subobjects admits an intersection" is used to *construct*. So the in-tree SAFT
assumes exactly what the book derives, and `Adjunction/SAFT.v:85-90` discloses
this honestly rather than mislabelling a proof. The verifier also identified the
genuinely proven SAFT content, which this issue should build on and not redo:
`cogenerator_canonical_monic` (`Adjunction/SAFT.v:223`), whose proof really does
consume `cog_separates`. Intersections/wide pullbacks remain 0 hits tree-wide,
which is why this issue depends on #445.

### Also covered by

Riehl, Epilogue §E.1, the restatement of the adjoint functor theorem for
locally presentable categories, printed p. 252 (PDF p. 272) — item
`riehl:E.1:thm-locally-presentable-adjoints`.

This is the Epilogue's one-line recall of §4.7 Theorem 4.7.17, already this
issue's subject in full; it adds no obligation. Phase-D confirmation worth
recording: the verifier's blind pass re-established that "locally presentable"
and "accessible" occur exactly once each in the tree, both inside the
`Adjunction/GAFT.v:122-127` header essay describing the Adámek–Rosický
sharpening as *external* context, and that there is no notion of a filtered
category, filtered/directed colimit, presentable or compact object, or
Ind-completion anywhere (the sole `filtered` hit, `Comonad/CoKleisli.v:81`, is a
stream metaphor). Both clauses are therefore unstatable as written, not merely
unproven — which is exactly why this issue's step 1 has to choose and disclose a
κ-smallness encoding before anything else can be said.

part: solution-set form of the representability criterion

### Also covered by

Riehl, Epilogue §E.1, the restatement of the representability criteria for
limit-preserving `Set`-valued functors, printed p. 252 (PDF p. 272) — item
`riehl:E.1:thm-representability-criteria`, the solution-set clause. (The
coseparating-set/intersections clause of the same item is recorded on #453.)

Phase-D sharpening for the implementer: the verifier confirmed that
`Class Representable` (`Functor/Representable.v:46`) **is never the conclusion of
any `Theorem`/`Lemma`/`Proposition`/`Corollary` in the tree** — it appears only
as its own definition, its coercion, and in prose — so this issue would supply
the first. It also disambiguated the nearest name collision:
`Theory/Profunctor/Adjunction.v:68`'s "representability criterion for
adjunctions" is a different result (`F ⊣ U ↔ Repr_left F ≅ Repr_right U`) and
must not be counted. Finally it verified that the natural proof route needs
**both** missing pieces this issue already plans — the global-elements
isomorphism `(1 ~{Sets}~> X) ≅ carrier X` and a bridge from `UniversalArrow` to
`Functor/Representable.v` — so neither can be assumed available.

### Also covered by

Riehl, Epilogue §E.1, the restatement of the representability criteria for
limit-preserving `Set`-valued functors, printed p. 252 (PDF p. 272) — item
`riehl:E.1:thm-representability-criteria`, the clause deriving representability
from a small coseparating set plus intersections of subobjects. (The
solution-set clause of the same item is recorded on #437.)

This is the corollary this issue already scopes ("every continuous functor into
sets on such a domain is representable"); no new obligation. It does, however,
make that corollary load-bearing rather than incidental: Riehl presents the
coseparator form as one of the two standard representability criteria, so it
should be exposed as a named result and not left implicit inside the SAFT proof.

### Also covered by

Riehl, Epilogue §E.1, the restatement of the properties of monadic functors,
printed p. 252 (PDF pp. 272–273) — item `riehl:E.1:thm-monadicity`, clauses (ii)
and (iii). (Clause (iv), cocompleteness from preservation of filtered colimits,
is recorded on #1010; clause (i), conservativity, is already in force in-tree.)

Phase-D sharpening: the verifier confirmed clause (i) really is present and in
a *stronger* form than Riehl states it — `Monad/Monadicity/Beck.v:264`
`creates_split_reflects_isos` derives conservativity from creation of `U`-split
coequalizers **alone**, with no left adjoint required, and the file's own header
at `:63-76` ("Conservativity is derived, not assumed") gives exactly that
argument; `:911` `monadic_creates` supplies `CreatesUSplitCoequalizers` for
`EM_Forget`, so a monadic forgetful functor's conservativity genuinely follows.
Against that, clauses (ii) and (iii) were independently confirmed absent: the
only creation notions in the tree are `CreatesUSplitCoequalizers`
(`Beck.v:164`), `em_forget_creates_split` (`BeckObjects.v`) and
`equivalence_creates_limits`/`_colimits` (`Theory/Equivalence/Limit.v:486`/`:584`,
about **equivalences**, not monadic functors), and grepping `Limit`/`Complete`
across all of `Monad/` returns only `Require` lines and comments — the `Monad/`
tree proves no (co)limit result at all.

### Also covered by

Riehl, Epilogue §E.1, the restatement of the properties of monadic functors,
printed p. 252 (PDF pp. 272–273) — item `riehl:E.1:thm-monadicity`, clause (iv):
if the base is locally small, complete and cocomplete and the monadic functor
preserves filtered colimits, the category of algebras has all small colimits.
(Clauses (ii)–(iii) are recorded on #1008.)

This is this issue's Theorem 5.6.12 in the Epilogue's compressed phrasing, so it
adds no obligation. Phase-D confirmation: the verifier independently re-checked

`Comonad/CoKleisli.v:81`), so clause (iv) is literally unstatable until this
issue's finitary/filtered vocabulary lands — a point worth keeping visible,
since it is the hypothesis, not the conclusion, that blocks.

append_block:
### Also covered by

Riehl, Epilogue §E.2, the roster of examples of symmetric monoidal categories,
printed p. 253 (PDF pp. 273–274) — item
`riehl:E.2:example-symmetric-monoidal`, clause (b): any category with finite
coproducts is symmetric monoidal with tensor the coproduct and unit the initial
object. (Clause (c) is recorded on #388, clause (d) on the new Riehl E.2
chain-complex issue, clause (e) on #772; clause (a) is already in force in-tree
as `CC_SymmetricMonoidal`.)

Phase-D sharpening that shortens the job: the verifier independently verified
the dualization arithmetic this issue's "one option" suggests. `Cocartesian C`
**is** notation for `@Cartesian (C^op)` (`Structure/Cocartesian.v:115`) and
`Initial C` for `@Terminal (C^op)` (`Structure/Initial.v:96`), and `Symmetric_op`
does sit at `Construction/Opposite/Monoidal.v:175` — so
`@CC_SymmetricMonoidal (C^op)` followed by `Symmetric_op` lands on `(C^op)^op = C`

part: clause (e): a commutative monoid as a discrete symmetric monoidal category
append_block:
### Also covered by

Riehl, Epilogue §E.2, the roster of examples of symmetric monoidal categories,
printed p. 253 (PDF pp. 273–274) — item
`riehl:E.2:example-symmetric-monoidal`, clause (e): a commutative monoid viewed
as a discrete category is a symmetric monoidal category in which every structure
isomorphism is an identity. (The roster's other clauses are recorded on #490,
#388, and the new Riehl E.2 chain-complex issue.)

Riehl frames this as a symmetric monoidal **category** on `DiscreteCat M` rather
than as a monoidal preorder, but on a discrete order the two are the same
obligation — the object-level equalities this issue already asks for
(associativity, unit, commutativity as equalities of objects, monotonicity
automatic) are exactly Riehl's "all structure isomorphisms are identities". This
issue's Work item 2 and its `Instance/Discrete/Monoidal.v` target cover it as
stated; no additional checklist item is needed. Phase-D confirmation:
`rg DiscreteCat | grep -i monoid` returns 0 hits, so nothing in-tree performs the
construction today.

### Also covered by

Riehl, Epilogue §E.2, the statement of the Mac Lane–Kelly coherence theorem for
monoidal categories, printed p. 254 (PDF p. 274) — item
`riehl:E.2:thm-monoidal-coherence`.

Riehl states it in the "every formal diagram of associators and unitors
commutes" form, which is this issue's `can_B` formulation; no new obligation.

Phase-D sharpening for the implementer, because it changes how the existing
in-tree lemmas should be regarded: the verifier initially leaned PARTIAL on the
strength of `Structure/Monoidal/Proofs.v`'s named consequences
(`triangle_identity_left`/`_right`, `inverse_pentagon_identity`,
`bimap_triangle_left`/`_right`, and Kelly's `unit_identity : λ_I ≈ ρ_I` at
`:344`), then rejected PARTIAL and settled on ABSENT for a reason the
implementation depends on: the theorem quantifies over **formal diagrams**, and
the library has no syntax of monoidal expressions to quantify over. There is no
free monoidal category (the only `Free…Monoidal` is `Construction/PROP`'s free
PROP on a *signature* with `nat` objects), no strictification, and the
reflective `Solver/` tower decides only composition/identity equations
(`rg -i tensor Solver/` → 0 hits). The existing Kelly lemmas are therefore
*downstream instances* of the theorem, not a proved fragment of it — they cannot
be reused as base cases of an induction that does not yet have a syntax to
induct on. Building `W` (this issue's dependency) is the unavoidable first step.

### Also covered by

Riehl, *Category Theory in Context*, 2nd ed., Epilogue §E.2, Theorem E.2.2 —
coherence for symmetric monoidal categories (attributed to Mac Lane and Kelly),
printed p. 254 (PDF p. 274) — item `riehl:E.2:thm2`.

Riehl's statement is the same-permutation form this issue's clause (a) already
scopes: two parallel canonical maps built from `α`, `λ`, `ρ` and `γ` agree
provided both sides induce the same permutation of the tensor factors.

Phase-D sharpening: the verifier confirmed that the symmetric coherence theorem
and its permutative corollary are stated in-tree **only as header prose**
(`Structure/Monoidal/Symmetric.v:47-56`), and that the results which do exist —
`hexagon_rotated` (`:118`), `bimap_braid` (`:137`), `braid_bimap_braid` (`:147`),
`braid_unit_left` (`Structure/Monoidal/Braided/Proofs.v:529`) and `braid_I_I`
(`:589`) — are individual instances of the conclusion, not a fragment of the
metatheorem. It also checked that `FreeCat_Symmetric`
(`Construction/PROP/Symmetric.v:75`) is the free symmetric strict monoidal
category on a *signature*, and that `Construction/PROP/Universal.v` is an
interpretation/extension universal property, **not** the coherence/faithfulness
statement — so the PROP development cannot be cited as covering this.

### Also covered by

Riehl, Epilogue §E.2, the corollary drawn from symmetric coherence: any two
functors `V^n ⟶ V` built iteratively from `⊗` and the unit, permuting and
parenthesizing their `n` inputs in any manner, are connected by a **unique**
natural isomorphism assembled from `α`, `λ`, `ρ` and `γ`; so a choice of
bracketing or ordering in defining an `n`-ary tensor is immaterial. Printed
p. 254 (PDF p. 274) — item `riehl:E.2:cor-nary-tensor`.

This is the working form in which the symmetric coherence theorem is actually
consumed, and the library already has two artifacts that would become its
special cases: `tfold_app` (`Theory/Multicategory/Representable.v:113`), an
explicit isomorphism `tfold ob (Γ ++ Δ) ≅ tfold ob Γ ⊗ tfold ob Δ` built from
`tensor_assoc`, and `perm_arrow` (`:543`), which realizes a permutation
**witness** `p : tperm Γ Δ` as a composite of braidings and associators.

The uniqueness half is what is missing, and the verifier pinned it precisely by
reading the library's own disclosure: `Theory/Multicategory.v:76-93` states
verbatim that `msym` is an action of `tperm` *witnesses*, that "two witnesses
realizing the same underlying permutation are not required to act identically",
and that "the descent lemmas themselves are not stated in-tree". That is exactly
the content Riehl's "unique" supplies, so the corollary is the missing lemma the
multicategory scope note is waiting for.

- [ ] (from Riehl §E.2) State the `n`-ary corollary explicitly: an `n`-ary
      tensor functor `V^n ⟶ V` given by a bracketing and an ordering, and the
      theorem that any two such are connected by a unique natural isomorphism
      built from the structure maps.
- [ ] (from Riehl §E.2) Derive witness-independence as the corollary's
      consequence: two `tperm` witnesses realizing the same permutation induce
      the same `perm_arrow` (the symmetric-group descent that
      `Theory/Multicategory.v:76-93` currently discloses as unproved), and
      repoint that scope note at the theorem.

### Also covered by

Riehl, Epilogue §E.3, the unit interval `I = [0,1]` as a topological space with
the Euclidean subspace topology, printed p. 255 (PDF p. 275) — item
`riehl:E.3:def-unit-interval`.

This issue's Work already names the obligation ("Interval infrastructure: this
needs a workable `[0,1]` — stdlib `Reals` (instance layer; any new stdlib axioms
must be enumerated in docs/AXIOMS.md) or a documented synthetic/constructive
substitute; the file header must state the choice and its cost"), so the
Epilogue adds no new requirement — but it raises the stakes, since Riehl's §E.3
then characterizes the same object by a universal property (the new Riehl E.3
issue), and the two descriptions should eventually be reconciled.

Phase-D confirmation: the library never imports the reals
(`rg 'Require.*Reals|Rdefinitions'` → 0 hits), there is no continuous map or
homeomorphism anywhere, and every `interval` hit in the tree is the interval
*category* `_2` (`Instance/Two.v`), the factorization category (`Instance/Fact.v`)
or the ordinal `ω` (`Instance/Omega.v`) — none topological.

### Also covered by

Riehl, Epilogue §E.3, paths in a topological space and the composition of paths,
printed p. 255 (PDF p. 275) — item `riehl:E.3:def-path`.

This issue's Work already covers paths as continuous maps out of the unit
interval and the reparametrized concatenation. One presentational difference
worth knowing: Riehl defines path composition through the "fattened interval"
`I ∨ I` obtained as a pushout of point-inclusions and a map out of it, rather
than by an explicit reparametrization formula. That wedge construction is being
built by the new Riehl E.3 issue (bipointed spaces and Freyd's terminal
coalgebra), so if that lands first this issue can take concatenation from it
instead of writing a formula; either route satisfies the requirement.

Phase-D note: `Structure/Pushout.v` already supplies general pushouts, so the
`I ∨ I` gluing square is expressible the moment a category of spaces exists —
the missing ingredient is the space, not the colimit.

### Also covered by

Riehl, Epilogue §E.3, the fundamental groupoid of a topological space (points as
objects, endpoint-fixing homotopy classes of paths as morphisms), printed p. 255
(PDF p. 275) — item `riehl:E.3:def-fundamental-groupoid`.

Identical in substance to this issue; no new obligation. Phase-D disambiguation
worth recording so a future reader does not mis-credit the library: the only
groupoid construction in-tree is `Construction/Groupoid.v:103`,
`Groupoid (C : Category) : Category`, the **core** (maximal subgroupoid, with
`hom := @Isomorphism C`) of a *category* — it takes a category, not a space, and
is a different construction from `Π₁`. "fundamental groupoid" appears in that
file only inside background prose about groupoids modelling homotopy 1-types,
and `rg -i 'homotopy class'` returns 0 relevant hits.

### Also covered by

Riehl, Epilogue §E.4, the (informal) definition of a site — a small category
equipped, for each object, with a specified **collection** of covering families
satisfying a weak pullback condition — printed p. 256 (PDF p. 276); item
`riehl:E.4:def-site`.

This issue's Work items 1 and 3 already cover the two deficits Riehl's phrasing
exposes: the vacuity of `coverage_condition` and the fact that a `Site` picks
**one** covering family per object rather than a collection of them. Phase-D

Riehl, *Category Theory in Context*, 2nd ed., Epilogue §E.5, Definition E.5.1 —

assumed fields. There is also no concrete `Abelian` instance anywhere in-tree,
so the class is inhabited only parametrically today.
